rows.claim: the payload carries the field-level diff (missing / unexpected / per-field expected-vs-observed)
rows.fix: ...and the field-level data: the observed and declared field lists, and per field the observed and declared types.

notes:
Slice S9c, spec.md 5659-6053. I changed no tracked file and ran no git command. My files are the probe script at /Users/miguel/.julia/dev/Redstone.jl/design/reports/20261124_doc_conformance/probes/S9c/probe.jl and the Julia output I ran from it. The probe ran about four times against W.

I counted 267 claims (counts) and listed 229 of them. The other 38 are ptr and why claims I counted without listing. I gave the 229 listed claims sequential IDs in document order, S9c-001 to S9c-229.

I raised 10 findings (S9c-032, 033, 051, 055, 062, 067, 132, 154, 186, 206):
- 032: x_projection is also probed at a Dual activation. Class drift.
- 033: the global-tracer activation is not built. Class deviation.
- 055: no synchronization after pre-materialization is false, because activation() locks on every lookup. Class deviation.
- 067: the cache entry holds decls, products and layout. It holds no compiled plans and no validated flag. Class deviation.
- 132 and 154: the quoted didactic message and the pin hint differ in wording from what the code renders. Class drift.
- 186: HandlerReturnKey shares no machinery with the bundle FieldError classification. Class drift.
- 206: the payload carries observed and declared field lists, not a missing/unexpected diff. Class drift.

I rate 051, 062 and 186 low confidence.

I had no unverifiable claims. I listed the lead for M_shaft (spec lines 5853 and 5884) as two ok placeholder rows, S9c-116 and S9c-131. The name is the Motor fixture's, test/fixtures.jl:163.

Two cases the procedure did not cover, left for the verifier:
- The glossary calls ProbeDual public, but the package has no export or public statements. I marked it ok because docs/src/api.md lists it.
- The claim "nothing numerical is ever cached" is arguable, because Activation.products holds probe values that seed the cells until first written. I marked it ok.

I checked the complete Julia code blocks in the range: the build(world; activations = (Float64, ProbeDual)) call, the ProbeDual definition and the two permuted return forms. All run as written.

The probe ran each of the following in a Julia process:
- A Dual activation of a continuous plus discrete model, counting which user functions it calls.
- The generated write, called directly with permuted, missing, extra and Int fields at Float64 and at ProbeDual.
- The handler and guard refusals.
- Walking, pinned and stripping leaves.
- A struct-valued port with a missing constructor.
